literal: day guisi: the late emperor-father was posthumously honored as Former Emperor; the late empress-dowager Lady Wang as Former Grand Consort;
idiomatic: On guisi day the late emperor, his father, was posthumously honored Former Emperor; Lady Wang, his mother, Former Grand Consort;

literal: the emperor’s younger brother Yongye was enfeoffed Prince of Gaomi; the imperial son Zishu was enfeoffed Prince of Bohai.
idiomatic: the emperor’s brother Yongye was made prince of Gaomi; the prince’s son Zishu, prince of Bohai.

literal: winter, tenth month, day renyin: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan set up Yuan Lang, administrator of Bohai, as emperor at Xindu.
idiomatic: On renyin day in the tenth month of winter Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan enthroned Yuan Lang, administrator of Bohai, at Xindu.

literal: spring, third month of the second year: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan defeated Erzhu Tianguang and others at Hanling.
idiomatic: In the third month of spring in the second year Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan routed Erzhu Tianguang and his allies at Hanling.

literal: The text is deficient.
idiomatic: The text is deficient.

literal: summer, fourth month, day xinsi: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan and the Deposed Emperor came to Mount Mang; he sent Wei Langen to comfort and instruct Luoyang and also observe the emperor’s character.
idiomatic: On xinsi day in the fourth month of summer Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan brought the Deposed Emperor to Mount Mang and sent Wei Langen to reassure Luoyang—and to take the measure of the man on the throne.

literal: Langen resented the emperor’s refined virtue; on his return he slandered him; in the end they followed Cui Ling’s counsel, deposed the emperor at Chongxun Buddhist temple, and set up Prince of Pingyang Xiu as emperor.
idiomatic: Langen envied the emperor’s quiet dignity; back at camp he poisoned Huan’s ear against him. They took Cui Ling’s advice, deposed the ruler at Chongxun Temple, and enthroned Xiu, prince of Pingyang.

literal: The emperor, having lost the throne, then composed a poem: "Crimson gates long breed sorrow; the purple apex is no place for fond play."
idiomatic: Stripped of the throne, he wrote a poem: "Crimson gates have long been worth dread; the purple summit is no toy for the heart."

literal: Overthrow and enthronement wait close at hand; thrice in one year the throne changes hands.
idiomatic: Ruin and renewal stand ready; three times in a single year the throne has changed hands.

literal: The age’s fortune is just like this—only cultivating truth in contemplation remains."
idiomatic: Fortune runs exactly so—only to cultivate truth in stillness is left."

literal: At the beginning of Taichang the emperor died in the outer office of the Gate Department; he was thirty-five years old.
idiomatic: Early in Taichang the Deposed Emperor died in the outer quarters of the Gate Department, aged thirty-five.

literal: Emperor Chu ordered the hundred offices to attend the mourning; the Grand Herald supervised the funeral; burial followed princely rite, with the addition of nine tassels, imperial carriage bells, yellow canopy, left great-banner, a hundred twenty halberds in formation, and full guard from the two guards and feathered guard.
idiomatic: Emperor Chu ordered the ministries to the funeral; the grand herald oversaw the rites. He was buried with princely honors plus nine tassels, imperial bells, yellow canopy, left great-banner, a hundred twenty halberds in formation, and escort from both palace guards and the feathered guard.

literal: The Deposed Emperor Houfei bore the taboo name Lang, styled Zhongzhe; he was the third son of Prince of Zhangwu Rong; his mother was Lady Cheng.
idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor Houfei bore the taboo name Lang, styled Zhongzhe. He was the third son of Prince of Zhangwu Rong; his mother was Lady Cheng.

literal: In youth he was famed as bright and perceptive.
idiomatic: As a boy he was praised for quick understanding.

literal: In the second year of Yongan he was recorder of the rear army headquarters of Prince of Lu Commandery of Si Province and commissioner with full powers, open-office staff major.
idiomatic: In the second year of Yongan he served as recorder of the rear-army headquarters of the prince of Lu in Si and as open-office staff major with commissioner’s powers.

literal: On day wuzi in the first month of the second year of Jianming under Yuan Ye he was made Administrator of Bohai in Ji Province.
idiomatic: On wuzi day in the first month of Jianming year two under Yuan Ye he became administrator of Bohai in Ji.

literal: When Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan raised the army of righteousness to punish violent rebels, he was set up and carried on the throne.
idiomatic: When Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan raised righteous troops to punish the tyrants, Lang was pushed onto the throne.

literal: eleventh month, day jisi: an edict said: "Royal measure is newly opened, ritual order just begun; official ranks issued remain under the old statutes."
idiomatic: On jisi day in the eleventh month an edict said: "The royal measure is newly opened and ritual order only begun; the ranks we issue still follow the old statutes."

literal: Yet men without understanding seized this chance; they wrongly added military rank and empty names with lofty posts, all saying they were conferred by the former court—hard to push back on principle."
idiomatic: Yet the witless seized the moment: they padded military rank and bought hollow titles, all claiming grants from the fallen court—titles hard to revoke in law.

literal: Unless strict regulations are made, there is no way to guard against false seizure."
idiomatic: Without stern rules there is no stopping the fraud."

literal: All who falsely added official titles and are denounced by others—punishment follows military law."
idiomatic: Whoever padded his title and is exposed shall be punished under military law."

literal: If on inspection the name does not fit the register, he is demoted to commoner and imprisoned for life."
idiomatic: If the rolls cannot verify the rank, he is reduced to commoner and imprisoned for life."

literal: day gengchen: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan led the army to attack Ye city.
idiomatic: On gengchen day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan marched against Ye.

literal: That year the people of Nan Yan city forced former Regional Inspector Liu Shiming to surrender the province to Xiao Yan; Yan sent his general Yuan Shu to enter and hold Qiao city.
idiomatic: That year the people of Nan Yan compelled Liu Shiming, former inspector, to hand the province to Xiao Yan; Yan’s general Yuan Shu seized Qiao.

literal: spring, first month, day renwu: Ye was taken; Regional Inspector Liu Dan was captured.
idiomatic: On renwu day in the first month of spring Ye fell; Liu Dan the inspector was taken.

literal: An edict ordered a universal promotion of four ranks for generals and soldiers; ninety-seven were enfeoffed marquis and given increased fiefs, each in differing measure.
idiomatic: An edict raised every soldier four ranks; ninety-seven men were made marquises with added fiefs, each according to merit.

literal: day guiwei: an edict said: "Since the revival in hardship, institutions were improvised; commandery and district officials were mostly acting supervisors and overseers."
idiomatic: On guiwei day an edict said: "Since our revival from chaos, law was makeshift; most commandery and district officers were only acting supervisors or overseers."

literal: Even where there were regular appointees, custom and teaching were not yet even.
idiomatic: Even regular appointees could not yet spread even rule.

literal: They looked on the remnant of Zhou as nothing but prey for the net.
idiomatic: They treated what remained of Zhou’s order as mere quarry for the hunter.

literal: We therefore rise early and sleep late, ever anxious in our breast.
idiomatic: We rise before dawn and sleep after dark, uneasy in heart.

literal: Let the relevant offices clearly add correction and punishment—this matches our intent."
idiomatic: Let the ministries punish without mercy—that is our will."

literal: second month, day xinhai: Emperor Xiaozhuang was given the posthumous title Emperor Wu the Cherishing.
idiomatic: On xinhai day in the second month Emperor Xiaozhuang received the posthumous title Emperor Wu the Cherishing.

literal: day jiazi: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan was made Grand Chancellor, Pillar Grand General, and Grand Preceptor; fief was increased by thirty thousand households, thirty thousand together with the former making sixty thousand.
idiomatic: On jiazi day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan was made grand chancellor, pillar grand general, and grand preceptor; his fief grew by thirty thousand households to sixty thousand in all.

literal: third month, day bingyin: Prince of Qi Wenxiang began his career as Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On bingyin day in the third month Prince of Qi Wenxiang first took office as grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day bingzi: Attendant, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Sun Teng was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On bingzi day Sun Teng, attendant, grand general of chariots and cavalry, and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day dingchou: the imperial carriage visited Ye.
idiomatic: On dingchou day the court moved to Ye.

literal: day yiyou: an edict ordered civil and military families from Xindu to come to Ye city.
idiomatic: On yiyou day an edict summoned officials’ families from Xindu to Ye.

literal: intercalary month, day yiwei: Pacifier of the North, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages, and State-Founding Earl of Boye Wei Jing was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On yiwei day in the intercalary month Wei Jing, pacifier of the north, grand master of splendid carriages, and state-founding earl of Boye, was made grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day bingshen: General of the Guard, Grand Master of Splendid Carriages with Golden Seal and Purple Cord Kudi Gan was made Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On bingshen day Kudi Gan, general of the guard and grand master of splendid carriages with golden seal and purple cord, was made grand general of chariots and cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day renyin: Erzhu Tianguang, Zhao, Dulu, Zhongyuan, and others encamped south of the Huan River.
idiomatic: On renyin day Erzhu Tianguang, Zhao, Dulu, Zhongyuan, and the rest camped south of the Huan.

literal: day guichou: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan halted at Zimo.
idiomatic: On guichou day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan encamped at Zimo.

literal: day gengshen: Erzhu Zhao led three thousand light horse in a night raid on Ye city, struck the west gate, failed to take it, and withdrew.
idiomatic: On gengshen day Erzhu Zhao struck Ye by night with three thousand light horse, hammered the west gate, failed, and fled.

literal: day renxu: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan greatly defeated Erzhu Tianguang and the other four Hu at Hanling; Deposed Emperor Qianfei’s Pacification-General Heba Sheng and Regional Inspector of Xu Province Du De surrendered at Chen.
idiomatic: On renxu day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan shattered Erzhu Tianguang and the four Hu allies at Hanling; Heba Sheng, pacification-general to Deposed Emperor Qianfei, and Du De, inspector of Xu, surrendered at Chen.

literal: Erzhu Zhao fled toward Bing Province; Zhongyuan ran to Dong Commandery; Tianguang and Dulu were about to go to Luoyang.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhao fled toward Bing; Zhongyuan ran to Dong commandery; Tianguang and Dulu turned for Luoyang.

literal: Grand Commander Husi Chun and Jia Xianzhi returned first by double march.
idiomatic: Grand commander Husi Chun and Jia Xianzhi raced ahead by forced march.

literal: summer, fourth month, day jiazi, new moon: Chun and others seized the He Bridge; fearing guilt they impeached themselves, then soon captured Tianguang and Dulu at the He Bridge.
idiomatic: On jiazi day, the new moon of the fourth month of summer, Chun’s party seized the He Bridge; though they impeached themselves for fear of blame, they soon took Tianguang and Dulu on the bridge.

literal: Northwest-route Grand Mobile Office Changsun Zhi, Commander Jia Xianzhi, and others led horse into the capital, seized Erzhu Shilong and Yanbo, beheaded them in the capital street, and sent Tianguang and Dulu imprisoned to Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan.
idiomatic: Changsun Zhi of the northwest grand mobile office and Jia Xianzhi and other commanders rode into Luoyang, seized Shilong and Yanbo, beheaded them in the market, and sent Tianguang and Dulu in bonds to Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan.

literal: day xinwei: Deposed Emperor Qianfei’s Pacification-General Hou Jing held the city and surrendered; he was then made Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Southern-Route Grand Mobile Office, and Regional Inspector of Ji Province.
idiomatic: On xinwei day Hou Jing, pacification-general to Deposed Emperor Qianfei, surrendered the city and was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, concurrent vice director of the Masters of Writing, southern-route grand mobile office, and inspector of Ji.

literal: day jiaxu: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry and Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wei Langen was made Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: On jiaxu day Wei Langen, grand general of chariots and cavalry and right vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made grand general of agile cavalry and equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day yihai: Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Central-Army Grand Commander Gao Sheng was made Concurrent Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and Northern-Route Grand Mobile Office, with discretionary authority.
idiomatic: On yihai day Gao Sheng, grand general of chariots and cavalry, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and central-army grand commander, was made concurrent vice director of the Masters of Writing and northern-route grand mobile office with full discretion.

literal: Erzhu Zhongyuan fled to Xiao Yan.
idiomatic: Erzhu Zhongyuan fled to Xiao Yan.

literal: Regional Inspector of Qing Province Erzhu Bi was killed by his subordinate Feng Shaolong; his head was sent to the capital.
idiomatic: Erzhu Bi, regional inspector of Qing, was killed by his officer Feng Shaolong; his head was sent to the capital.

literal: day bingzi: Deposed Emperor Qianfei’s Pacification-General of the East Xin Yong and Right General and Grand Commander of Jian Province Zhang Yue held their cities and surrendered.
idiomatic: On bingzi day Xin Yong, pacification-general of the east to Deposed Emperor Qianfei, and Zhang Yue, right general and grand commander of Jian, surrendered their cities.

literal: day xinsi: the imperial carriage reached Heyang and yielded the throne at a separate residence.
idiomatic: On xinsi day the court reached Heyang and the emperor abdicated at a side lodge.

literal: fifth month of the first year of Taichang: he was enfeoffed Prince of Anding Commandery, fief ten thousand households.
idiomatic: In the fifth month of Taichang year one he was enfeoffed prince of Anding with ten thousand households.

literal: Later, because of a crime, he died in the outer office of the Gate Department; he was twenty years old.
idiomatic: Later, condemned for crime, he died in the outer quarters of the Gate Department, aged twenty.

literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was buried at Wild Horse Mound southwest of Ye.
idiomatic: In Yongxi year two he was buried at Wild Horse Mound southwest of Ye.

literal: Emperor Chu bore the taboo name Xiu, styled Xiaze; he was the third son of Prince of Guangping Wu and Mu Huai; his mother was Lady Li.
idiomatic: Emperor Chu bore the taboo name Xiu, styled Xiaze. He was the third son of Prince of Guangping Wu and Mu, Huai; his mother was Lady Li.

literal: By nature he was deep and grave, spoke little, and loved martial affairs.
idiomatic: He was grave and sparing of speech, and loved the arts of war.

literal: He was first enfeoffed Duke of Ruyang Commandery with an open state and appointed direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant; he was transferred to vice director of the secretariat.
idiomatic: First enfeoffed state-founding duke of Ruyang, he was made direct-palace scattered cavalier attendant, then vice director of the secretariat.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was made scattered cavalier attendant; soon he was transferred to pacifier of the east and concurrent minister of supreme rejoicings; again he was made pacifier of the east and director of the imperial clan.
idiomatic: Early in Jianyi he became scattered cavalier attendant, then pacifier of the east and concurrent minister of supreme rejoicings, then pacifier of the east and director of the imperial clan.

literal: In the third year of Yongan he was enfeoffed Prince of Pingyang.
idiomatic: In the third year of Yongan he was made prince of Pingyang.

literal: At the beginning of Putai he was transferred to attendant, pacifier of the east, [5] equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing; he was again given attendant and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: Early in Putai he became attendant, pacifier of the east, [5] equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and concurrent right vice director of the Masters of Writing; soon he added attendant and left vice director.

literal: summer, fourth month of the second year of Zhongxing: the Prince of Anding, because he was remote in kinship, did not satisfy the heart of the realm; he asked to yield the great throne.
idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer in Zhongxing year two the prince of Anding, knowing himself too remote in blood to hold the realm’s loyalty, offered to abdicate.

literal: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan met with the hundred officials in council; all said the High Ancestor could not be without posterity; together they upheld the prince.
idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan convened the ministers; all said the dynasty could not lack Gaozu’s line—and together they pressed Xiu forward.

literal: day wuzi: he took the throne outside the eastern suburb, entered by the Dongyang and Yunlong gates, presided at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate in the front palace, and the hundred officials paid court congratulation.
idiomatic: On wuzi day he took the throne outside the eastern suburb, entered through the Dongyang and Yunlong gates, sat in the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, and received the court’s homage.

literal: When the rites were done he ascended the Changhe Gate and issued an edict: "Decline and peace follow in turn; abolition and establishment each have their season; the dark heaven hides nothing, spirits cannot instruct."
idiomatic: The rites finished, he mounted the Changhe Gate and proclaimed: "Fortune and ruin take turns; thrones fall and rise by season; heaven keeps no secret, and spirits cannot warn what men refuse to see."

literal: Great Wei inherits Heaven’s stem; virtue spreads through the realm, enfolding the nine domains, reaching beside the three luminaries.
idiomatic: Great Wei holds heaven’s mandate; its virtue fills the realm, gathering the nine domains and shining beside sun, moon, and stars.

literal: Yet heaven sent down calamity; fortune trod through many hardships; ritual and music collapsed, statutes and models were drowned.
idiomatic: Yet heaven sent calamity; hardship followed hardship; ritual and music broke apart, law and pattern sank in flood.

literal: Majestic was the Zhou house—cut down by barbarian raiders;
idiomatic: The Zhou house stood in glory—then barbarian raiders hewed it down;

literal: solemn the clear temple—about to become rank grass.
idiomatic: the clear temple stood in awe—soon to be only wild grass.

literal: Hu and Jie seized the moment and unleashed their blind cruelty, killing rulers and princes, flaying the realm inside and out.
idiomatic: Hu and Jie seized their hour and poured out blind cruelty—killing emperors and kings, flaying the realm within and without.

literal: They vied in the will to devour and did not know the heart of drunken repletion.
idiomatic: They competed to swallow all and never knew when greed was sated.

literal: Since the age of writing began, there has never been the like!
idiomatic: Since records began, nothing like it has been seen!

literal: Grand Chancellor Prince of Bohai was loyal to the root of the dynasty, his essence piercing the white sun; he raised the banner of righteousness to wash away the nation’s shame.
idiomatic: The grand chancellor, prince of Bohai, stayed loyal to the dynasty’s root, his resolve bright as noon; he raised the righteous banner to wash away national shame.

literal: Thus at Guang’a the army—tiger and leopard seized their breath;
idiomatic: At Guang’a his host struck—foes bold as tiger and leopard lost their breath;

literal: at Ye the host—metal walls and moats lost their strength.
idiomatic: at Ye the walls of metal and moat failed.

literal: Lately the four Hu came in concert—a host indeed numerous; they drove the realm’s armies and mustered all Hua and Rong’s keen blades.
idiomatic: Lately the four Hu marched together—a multitude indeed; they drove the empire’s armies and sharpened every blade of Chinese and barbarian.

literal: Drums and bells had barely crossed when in one morning all was swept away; the chief culprit yielded his head, the great enemy was seized.
idiomatic: Drums had scarcely sounded when one morning swept them away; the chief culprit lost his head, the great foe was bound.

literal: Banners were raised to cross the river and sweep Yi and Luo clean; gentry and people rested secure, the old order unlost.
idiomatic: Standards crossed the river and cleared Yi and Luo; people settled in peace, the old order intact.

literal: The altars were in peril yet became safe again; the great foundation was broken yet built anew.
idiomatic: Altars tottered yet stood; the great foundation broke yet rose again.

literal: We, entrusted with the imperial body, unworthily meet the age’s push; we reverently grasp the precious chart and inherit this great enterprise.
idiomatic: We, set on the imperial frame, unworthily receive the age’s push; we hold the sacred chart and take up this great work.

literal: To place our slight person above kings and dukes is like crossing deep water without knowing the ford.
idiomatic: To set our slight self above kings and dukes is to wade deep water with no ford in sight.

literal: We think to share this blessed celebration with the hundred millions; a general amnesty may be declared throughout the realm.
idiomatic: We mean to share this blessing with the millions; let there be a general amnesty.

literal: The second year of Zhongxing is changed to the first year of Taichang."
idiomatic: Zhongxing year two becomes Taichang year one."

literal: An edict restored former Censor-in-Chief Fan Zihu to his original post, made him concurrent left vice director of the Masters of Writing and southeastern-route grand mobile office, and ordered Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Regional Inspector of Xu Province Du De to attack Yuan Shu.
idiomatic: An edict restored Fan Zihu, former censor-in-chief, to office, made him concurrent left vice director and southeastern-route grand mobile office, and ordered Du De, equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and inspector of Xu, against Yuan Shu.

literal: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan submitted a memorial: households of the righteous army wrongly confiscated by the Erzhu clan were all to be wholly remitted.
idiomatic: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan memorialized that families of righteous-army men wrongly seized by the Erzhu should be fully restored.

literal: Because the age had changed, the emperor again made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan grand chancellor, pillar of heaven grand general, and grand preceptor; he was to inherit the post of regional inspector of Ding Province; fief was increased by ninety thousand, together with the former making one hundred fifty thousand households.
idiomatic: With the throne renewed, the emperor again made Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan grand chancellor, pillar of heaven grand general, and grand preceptor, hereditary inspector of Ding; his fief grew by ninety thousand households to one hundred fifty thousand in all.

literal: day gengyin: Prince of Qi Wenxiang was given attendant and commissioner with full powers; the rest remained as before.
idiomatic: On gengyin day Prince of Qi Wenxiang received attendant and commissioner with full powers; other posts stood unchanged.

literal: day renchen: Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan returned to Ye; the imperial carriage saw him off in farewell at Mount Ganfu.
idiomatic: On renchen day Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan returned to Ye; the court took leave at Mount Ganfu.

literal: fifth month, day bingshen: Deposed Emperor Qianfei, Prince of Guangling, died.
idiomatic: On bingshen day in the fifth month Deposed Emperor Qianfei, prince of Guangling, died.

literal: Grand Tutor Prince of Huaiyang Xin was made Grand Preceptor and enfeoffed Prince of Pei Commandery;
idiomatic: Xin, grand tutor and prince of Huaiyang, was made grand preceptor and enfeoffed prince of Pei;

literal: Minister of Works Prince of Zhao Commandery Chen was made Grand Guardian;
idiomatic: Chen, minister of works and prince of Zhao, was made grand guardian;

literal: Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Prince of Qinghe Dan—Equal in Honor to the Three Preceptors;
idiomatic: Dan, prince of Qinghe, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, was made equal in honor to the three preceptors;

literal: [6] Bearer of the Staff, Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Commissioner with Full Powers Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies, Governor of Si Province, Prince of Nanyang Baoju was made Grand Preceptor;
idiomatic: [6] Baoju, prince of Nanyang, bearer of the staff, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, commissioner with full powers equal in honor to the Three Excellencies, and governor of Si, was made grand preceptor;

literal: Attendant, Grand Guardian, Recorder of Secretariat Affairs Changsun Zhi was made Grand Tutor;
idiomatic: Changsun Zhi, attendant, grand guardian, and recorder of secretariat affairs, was made grand tutor;

literal: Attendant, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Yuan Luo—Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies and Director of the Masters of Writing;
idiomatic: Yuan Luo, attendant, grand general of agile cavalry, and left vice director of the Masters of Writing, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies and director of the Masters of Writing;

literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry and Minister of Personnel Yuan Shijun—Equal in Honor to the Three Excellencies.
idiomatic: Yuan Shijun, grand general of agile cavalry and minister of personnel, was made equal in honor to the Three Excellencies.

literal: day wuxu: because Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan firmly declined, he was permitted to resign the pillar of heaven grand general post; fief was reduced by fifty thousand households; the rest all remained as before.
idiomatic: On wuxu day, because Prince of Qi Duke Xianwu Huan declined firmly, he was allowed to lay down pillar of heaven grand general; his fief was cut by fifty thousand households; all else stood.

literal: day xinchou: former Minister of Works Gao Gan’ou was again made Minister of Works.
idiomatic: On xinchou day former minister of works Gao Gan’ou was restored as minister of works.
